title: FlashAttention: why exact attention got faster by moving fewer bytes
summary: Why attention on a GPU is limited by memory traffic rather than arithmetic, and how FlashAttention computes exact attention without ever writing the N-by-N score table: tiling, the online softmax's running maximum and sum, and recomputation in the backward pass. Then four versions in four years, each chasing a bottleneck that moved, from HBM to non-matmul FLOPs to the exponential unit.

topics: deep dive: FlashAttention and why attention is memory-bound
concepts_taught: compute-bound versus memory-bound GPU operations: HBM versus on-chip SRAM, arithmetic intensity, and why matrix multiplies can be 99.8% of a BERT layer's arithmetic but 61% of its runtime (Ivanov et al.), with the memory wall (Wulf and McKee 1994) as lineage

FlashAttention's tiling: exact attention computed block by block in SRAM using the online softmax (running max and sum with rescaling, Milakov and Gimelshein 2018), so the N-by-N score table is never written to HBM; memory linear in sequence length, compute still quadratic

recomputation instead of storage in FlashAttention's backward pass: keep the output and per-row softmax statistics, rebuild score blocks on chip — more FLOPs (75.2 vs 66.6 GFLOPs on GPT-2 medium) but ~9x less HBM traffic and ~5.7x faster; IO complexity Θ(N²d²/M) versus Θ(Nd + N²)

the moving bottleneck across FlashAttention-2/3/4 and Flash-Decoding: non-matmul FLOPs (16x costlier on A100), parallelism over sequence and over the KV axis at decode, the exponential unit (989 vs 3.9 TFLOPS on H100), and on Blackwell software-emulated exponentials and threshold-based lazy rescaling
